hints: Focus on what the area to the right of an activation energy mark really means on a Boltzmann curve.
Notice which curve is flatter with a lower peak and more particles at high energy, that must be the hotter 35 °C sample.
For each case, start at the correct $E_a$ line and add up all the shaded area under the correct temperature curve to the right of it.
walkthrough:
**Recall what Boltzmann area means**

Think of the curve as showing how energy is shared out. Only particles to the right of the $E_a$ line have $E \ge E_a$ and can react on collision.

Rule:
$$\text{particles able to react} = \text{area under that temperature curve to the right of } E_a$$

**Identify the 25 °C and 35 °C curves**

Raising temperature flattens the peak and pushes more particles into the high energy tail, but total area stays the same.

So the taller, narrower peak is $25^\circ\text{C}$ and the lower, broader curve with the bigger high-energy tail is $35^\circ\text{C}$.

**Count for catalysed reaction at 25 °C**

A catalyst lowers $E_a$, so start at the left line labelled $E_a$ catalysed. Follow the $25^\circ\text{C}$ (lower tail) curve to the right.

That total area is made of the light block plus the dark tail:
$$y + z$$

**Count for uncatalysed reaction at 35 °C**

Without a catalyst $E_a$ is higher, so start at the right line labelled $E_a$ uncatalysed. Now follow the $35^\circ\text{C}$ (upper tail) curve to the right.

That total area is the upper tail plus the common tail:
$$x + z$$

**Match to the table**

Catalysed at $25^\circ\text{C}$ gives $y+z$. Uncatalysed at $35^\circ\text{C}$ gives $x+z$. That combination is the correct row.

options.A: Not correct. w + x + y + z would be far too large, it adds areas from both temperature curves together. Also z alone is only the part under the 25 °C curve beyond $E_a$ uncatalysed, not the larger 35 °C tail.
options.B: Half right but half wrong. x + z is correct for the 35 °C uncatalysed case, but w + x + y + z incorrectly sums both curves for the catalysed case instead of just the area under the 25 °C curve to the right of $E_a$ catalysed.
options.C: Half right but half wrong. y + z is correct for the 25 °C catalysed case, but z alone misses the extra x area. At 35 °C there are more particles beyond $E_a$ uncatalysed than at 25 °C, so you need x + z.
options.D: Correct. At 25 °C, all particles to the right of the lower $E_a$ catalysed line can react, which is y + z. At 35 °C, all particles to the right of the higher $E_a$ uncatalysed line can react, which is the larger tail x + z.
